replacements.replacement: The MIT AI Incident Tracker classifies incident records from the AI Incident Database by risk, cause, harm, severity, and other dimensions.

The AI Incident Tracker adds structure to reports in the AI Incident Database. Arcola AI’s classification pipeline assigns risk and harm categories so researchers can examine the composition of reported incidents. Changes in database counts can reflect reporting and coverage as well as underlying events.

The charts show incident counts and distributions across risk domains, causal classifications, and harm assessments. Some views count multiple assignments per incident, so their shares describe assignments rather than distinct incidents. These patterns describe the database; they do not establish how common AI harms are across society.
Among records dated 2021–2025, the share with the primary subdomain “4.3 Fraud, scams, and targeted manipulation” rose each year, from 3 of 80 (3.75%) in 2021 to 192 of 452 (42.48%) in 2025.

replacements.replacement: A June 2026 pilot compared eight models with consensus labels from two reviewers on 10 incidents. Some model and prompt combinations met the human agreement baseline on that sample. Prompt refinements used the same incidents, so these results require testing on a separate sample. The study does not establish the accuracy of all current classifications; the September 27 export predominantly uses a model not evaluated in that pilot.
replacements.scope_note: The pilot evaluated Harm Severity across ten dimensions, EU AI Act risk level, and causal, domain and subdomain taxonomies. It did not establish accuracy of the current thirteen-dimension harm classification.
